extracted.intended_audience: brand managers, marketing and product strategists, social media/community managers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for companies planning to use crowdsourcing or social co-creation to develop or change a brand logo, focusing on strategy, community engagement, incentives, and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tap into your online community before deciding on a redesign
rubrics_metrics.description: Use your existing online community to see if they think a new logo is necessary before committing to a change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post recommends a simple inquiry on Facebook or Twitter to gauge sentiment; from the Gap example it seemed clear fans were fine with the legacy blue box logo. This is a diagnostic step to avoid unnecessary redesigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent about incentives and avoid soliciting unpaid 'spec work'
rubrics_metrics.description: If you invite fans or designers to submit ideas, clearly specify incentives/compensation and avoid requesting speculative unpaid work under the guise of crowdsourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gap asked fans to submit ideas but 'did not provide any further details... particularly with regard to incentives or compensation,' which amplified dissent. The guidance is to state incentives up front and not to ask for spec work without clear terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include fans in the selection process rather than presenting a finished choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than selecting a logo and then hoping for approval, involve empowered fans in choosing among options during the selection phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This could be done via input mechanisms or a smaller private online community recruited through existing social media channels. Providing fans the opportunity to help choose increases buy-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a smaller private online community or moderated panel for selection/testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a controlled or private community (either provided by a community vendor or recruited from your channels) to test options and get constructive feedback during selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post suggests a private community as an alternative to open, ad-hoc solicitation — it can provide structured, actionable input during selection without exposing the process prematurely to broad public backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run a proper co-creation contest with appropriate incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: If pursuing co-creation, conduct a structured contest up front that offers clear incentives and engages a wide-ranging audience of creatives and fans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A properly run co-creation contest avoids misfires like Gap's post-hoc crowdsourcing. The contest should be designed to attract contributors, offer proper rewards, and be transparent about rules and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage co-creation as a marketable attribute to build positive PR and reduce backlash
rubrics_metrics.description: When consumers are included in logo development, the resulting ‘co-created with our customers’ claim can generate positive media attention and make stakeholders more accepting of the final design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including consumers creates a marketable attribute and can quell social media backlash because empowered customers have been made aware of and involved in the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a clear crowdsourcing strategy and choose the right timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a distinct strategy for how to conduct crowdsourcing or co-creation and ensure the timing of such projects is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post criticizes Gap's 'distinct lack of strategy' and the assertion that it 'wasn't the right project at the right time for crowdsourcing.' Planning strategy and timing up front helps avoid reversals and public missteps.
